jordan: rolling a FP8 canary on H100+L40S farm to validate kernel selector + TE configs. saw a weird p95 spike when microbatching long contexts (>4k).

sam: details? numbers?

jordan: test profile: baseline int8 (stable) -> p95 68ms; FP8 candidate -> p95 145ms, throughput -18% on L40S for same QPS.

lee: any logs? kernel fallback traces?

jordan: yes, trace shows repeated kernel handoff: `quant_kernel_select -> te_path -> fallback_int8` and a KV cache miss storm. snippet:
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:10Z] select_kernel(fp8, h100, seqlen=4096) -> transformer_engine: path_ok
[2026-03-12T14:02:10Z] te_execute: kernel_sync_timeout -> fallback=int8
[2026-03-12T14:02:10Z] kv_cache: evict_rate +3.2x -> miss_spike
```

maria: looks like warmup + occupancy thrash. microbatching shape? batch shapes?

jordan: microbatch shapes: mostly 1->4 dynamic shapes, average tokens/request 3400. config:
```
TRANSFORMER_ENGINE_FALLBACK=true
TE_PRECOMPILE=queued
BATCH_SHAPE_AUTOSCALER=on
KV_REPLAY=2
```

ciara: is this reproducible with a controlled load (no network/noisy neighbor)?

jordan: reproducible locally on bench nodes when we flip `--fp8-enable` on same model. runs fine on short contexts (<512). long contexts trigger kernel handshake jitter.

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: job=fp8-sanwave-canary-20260312, metric=p95_latency, delta=+112ms, severity=high

sam: hypothesis: FP8 TE kernels have higher headroom for occupancy but failover path cost (nvfuser->te->fallback) creates stalls; KV cache eviction caused by temporary memory pressure on FP8 path since quantized KV sizes differ.

lee: suggestion: 1) force single kernel path (disable fallback) in canary to isolate cost of TE kernels; 2) bump kv cache size + increase prefix caching TTL; 3) increase microbatch slot pooling to smooth occupancy.

jordan: tried 1) disable fallback -> p95 improved to 90ms but saw incorrect outputs on a small eval set (calibration issue). 2) bumping KV mem + prefix TTL -> p95 down to 110ms, but still worse than int8. 3) slot pooling -> reduces variance but not median.

maria: calibration could be why disabling fallback gave wrong outputs. can you attach a diff between fp8-calib-v1/v2?

jordan: uploaded to artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/fp8/sanitywave/calib-diffs.tar.gz

ciara: can we try hybrid kernel: use fp8 for matmuls, int8 for softmax/gelu? whether TE supports that mix?

lee: transformer engine supports mixed-kernel via `TE_PARTIAL_QUANT=matmul` flag on our builds. could try quickly.

sam: also try forcing KV to be stored in host pinned memory path (slower but less eviction thrash) to confirm memory pressure cause.

jordan: quick notes from last run:
- mix-kernel (matmul fp8, others int8) -> p95 78ms on H100, 115ms on L40S
- pinned-KV -> p95 85ms but throughput -7%
- disable fallback + better calib -> correctness fixed for v2 -> p95 72ms on H100, but L40S still 105ms

maria: seems H100 responds better to fp8 TE kernels; L40S needs different TE kernel selection heuristics. maybe the kernel selector is picking a TE kernel tuned for H100 occupancy, but L40S needs lower blocksize.

ciara: action items:
- sam: add kernel selector rule: if device==L40S & seq_len>2048 -> prefer nvfuser-int8 or smaller TE blocksize
- lee: expose `TE_PARTIAL_QUANT` to canary config and try hybrid
- jordan: run 3x controlled load bench with KV pinned vs default, attach traces
- maria: run eval set to validate calibration v2

sam: I'll also add telemetry to record kernel handoff latency and kv-eviction rates per-request in the canary trace.

jordan: thanks — will run jobs now. ping me if you want access.

ciara: good set. if L40S still fails, we should roll back FP8 on L40S and keep H100 canary going.

perf-bot: canary-status update: fp8-sanwave-canary-20260312 -> partial_pass (H100 green, L40S fail)

sam: noted. I'll prepare a follow-up with selector patch and a real quick AB test tomorrow.

lee: FYI adding `TE_BLOCKSIZE_HINT=16` on L40S improved microbench matmul by +9% in synthetic runs.

jordan: thanks all. will post final logs here when runs finish. :thumbsup:
